subject.title: Orphaned lock files not cleared on gateway restart when PID matches current process

question: What liveness policy should OpenClaw use before reclaiming a live same-PID session JSONL lock that is no longer making progress?
rationale: Current code can reclaim some untracked same-PID locks, but stronger live-lock reclamation changes the safety boundary between recovery and stealing an active transcript writer.

options.title: Define a liveness-backed lock policy
options.body: Add an owner-approved heartbeat, lease, or equivalent progress signal and prove startup cleanup, restart recovery, active-writer preservation, and stuck-lock recovery together.

options.title: Keep the conservative policy
options.body: Treat current startup/acquisition reclaim as sufficient and accept that live same-PID lock timeouts remain bounded only by existing watchdog and operator recovery behavior.

options.title: Adopt a refreshed narrow PR
options.body: Use the linked fork PR only as source material after it is rebased, made mergeable, stripped of unrelated files, and proven not to regress active in-process writes.

recommendation.title: Define a liveness-backed lock policy
recommendation.body: Add an owner-approved heartbeat, lease, or equivalent progress signal and prove startup cleanup, restart recovery, active-writer preservation, and stuck-lock recovery together.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the broadest recent history on the session-write-lock files and is the best available routing owner for the recovery safety policy.
